# Diagonal Phase Transition Incompleteness for Closure Self-Models

This file formalizes the **diagonal phase transition incompleteness theorem**:
a critical point in the diagonal free energy of a closure self-model certifies
the existence of an infinite family of internally irreducible self-descriptions.

## Mathematical Overview

A **closure self-model** is a type `M` equipped with:
- A **free energy function** `freeEnergy : ℝ → M → ℝ` assigning thermodynamic
  cost at inverse temperature `β` to each element.
- A **complexity measure** `complexity : M → ℕ` capturing the internal description
  length of elements.
- A **thermodynamic bridge axiom** asserting that if every infinite family of
  `M`-elements has uniformly bounded complexity, then the diagonal free energy
  (the supremum of free energies over all elements) is everywhere differentiable.

The fundamental axiom encodes a deep principle: phase transitions (non-differentiable
points in the free energy) can only arise when there exist infinite families that
resist uniform compression. The main theorem extracts the contrapositive:

> **Diagonal Phase Transition Incompleteness:**
> If the diagonal free energy has a critical point (non-differentiable point),
> then there exists an infinite family of elements that cannot be uniformly
> compressed within the closure mechanism.

This upgrades classical incompleteness from a static impossibility statement
to a quantitative capacity law: thermodynamic criticality certifies the
existence of infinitely many internally irreducible self-descriptions.

## Main Results

* `HasCriticalPoint` — definition of critical points for real functions
* `ClosureSelfModel` — the abstract closure self-model typeclass
* `diagFreeEnergy` — the diagonal free energy function
* `UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure` — uniform compressibility predicate
* `DiagonalEntropyBarrier` — the entropy barrier property
* `critical_point_contrapositive_bridge` — the key bridge lemma
* `not_forall_imp_exists_and_neg` — classical logic extraction helper
* `diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness` — **the main theorem**
* `diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness_weak` — weaker existential form
* `diagonal_entropy_barrier_iff` — characterization of the entropy barrier
* `DiagSubcriticalAnalyticFailure` — sharper analytic failure predicate
* `diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness_of_nonanalytic` — sharper variant
* `critical_point_yields_infinite_diagonal_irreducibles` — quantitative form

## References

* Gödel, K. — Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze (1931)
* Lawvere, F.W. — Diagonal arguments and cartesian closed categories (1969)
-/

import Mathlib

open Classical Set

universe u

/-! ## §1. Fundamental Definitions -/

/-- A **critical point** of a real-valued function `f`: a point where `f` fails
    to be differentiable. In the thermodynamic setting, this models a phase
    transition where the free energy develops a singularity (e.g., a cusp or
    discontinuity in a derivative). -/
def HasCriticalPoint (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ β₀ : ℝ, ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ f β₀

/-- A **closure self-model** is a type equipped with thermodynamic structure:

    - `freeEnergy β m`: the free energy at inverse temperature `β` for element `m`
    - `complexity m`: an integer complexity measure of element `m`

    The fundamental axiom `ax_uniform_compression_implies_no_criticality` asserts
    that universal uniform compressibility of infinite families precludes critical
    points in the diagonal free energy. Concretely: if every infinite family of
    `M`-elements has uniformly bounded complexity, then the function
    `β ↦ sup_m freeEnergy(β, m)` is everywhere differentiable.

    This axiom encodes the principle that thermodynamic phase transitions in
    self-referential systems can only occur when there exist infinite families
    that resist uniform compression — the diagonal analogue of incompleteness
    phenomena. -/
class ClosureSelfModel (M : Type u) where
  /-- Free energy at inverse temperature `β` for element `m`. -/
  freeEnergy : ℝ → M → ℝ
  /-- Complexity measure (internal description length) of an element. -/
  complexity : M → ℕ
  /-- **Thermodynamic bridge axiom.** If every infinite family of `M`-elements
      has uniformly bounded complexity, then the diagonal free energy
      `β ↦ ⨆ m, freeEnergy β m` is everywhere differentiable.

      This is the core physical principle: universal compressibility forces
      the diagonal free energy into the subcritical (analytic) regime. -/
  ax_uniform_compression_implies_no_criticality :
    (∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
      ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n, complexity (φ n) ≤ C) →
    ∀ β₀ : ℝ, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun β => ⨆ m : M, freeEnergy β m) β₀

/-! ## §2. Derived Thermodynamic Notions -/

/-- The **diagonal free energy** of a closure self-model `M`:
    the supremum over all elements of their free energy at inverse temperature `β`.

    This function captures the worst-case thermodynamic cost of self-description
    across all elements of the model. Critical points of this function correspond
    to phase transitions in the model's diagonal self-evaluation capacity. -/
noncomputable def diagFreeEnergy (M : Type u) [ClosureSelfModel M] : ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun β => ⨆ m : M, ClosureSelfModel.freeEnergy β m

/-- **Uniform compressibility within closure**: a family `φ : ℕ → M` is
    uniformly compressible if there exists a uniform bound `C` on the
    complexity of all elements in the family.

    This captures the idea that the entire family can be "compressed" to
    descriptions of bounded length within the model's closure mechanism. -/
def UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure (M : Type u) [ClosureSelfModel M]
    (φ : ℕ → M) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n, ClosureSelfModel.complexity (φ n) ≤ C

/-- **Compressibility within a specific bound**: the family `φ` has all
    complexities bounded by `C`. This is the quantitative refinement of
    `UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure`. -/
def CompressibleWithinClosureBound (M : Type u) [ClosureSelfModel M]
    (φ : ℕ → M) (C : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, ClosureSelfModel.complexity (φ n) ≤ C

/-- The **diagonal entropy barrier**: the property that every infinite family
    of `M`-elements is incompressible (has unbounded complexity).

    When this barrier holds, the model has sufficient "room" for all self-referential
    data. When it fails, some infinite family can be uniformly compressed,
    indicating a thermodynamic anomaly. -/
def DiagonalEntropyBarrier (M : Type u) [ClosureSelfModel M] : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
    ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ

/-- **Subcritical analytic failure**: the diagonal free energy has a critical
    point at some specific inverse temperature `βc`. This is the sharper
    form of `HasCriticalPoint` that identifies the specific transition point. -/
def DiagSubcriticalAnalyticFailure (M : Type u) [ClosureSelfModel M] : Prop :=
  ∃ βc : ℝ, ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ (diagFreeEnergy M) βc

/-- Witness family type alias for diagonal constructions. -/
def DiagonalWitnessFamily (M : Type u) [ClosureSelfModel M] : Type u := ℕ → M

/-! ## §3. Equivalences and Reformulations -/

/-- `UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure` is equivalent to the existence of a
    bound satisfying `CompressibleWithinClosureBound`. -/
theorem uniformlyCompressible_iff_exists_bound
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] {φ : ℕ → M} :
    UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ ↔
      ∃ C : ℕ, CompressibleWithinClosureBound M φ C := by
  rfl

/-- Unbounded complexity implies non-uniform-compressibility. -/
theorem not_uniformlyCompressible_of_unbounded
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] {φ : ℕ → M} :
    (∀ C : ℕ, ¬ CompressibleWithinClosureBound M φ C) →
    ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ := by
  intro h ⟨C, hC⟩
  exact h C hC

/-- `DiagSubcriticalAnalyticFailure` is equivalent to `HasCriticalPoint`
    applied to the diagonal free energy. -/
theorem diagSubcriticalAnalyticFailure_iff_hasCriticalPoint
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] :
    DiagSubcriticalAnalyticFailure M ↔ HasCriticalPoint (diagFreeEnergy M) := by
  rfl

/-- The diagonal entropy barrier holds if and only if every infinite family
    is incompressible. (This is definitional but stated for API clarity.) -/
theorem diagonal_entropy_barrier_iff
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] :
    DiagonalEntropyBarrier M ↔
      ∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
        ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ := by
  rfl

/-! ## §4. Classical Logic Helpers -/

/-- Classical extraction: the negation of a universal implication yields an
    existential conjunction with negation. This is the key logical maneuver
    for converting "not all infinite families are compressible" into
    "some infinite family is incompressible." -/
theorem not_forall_imp_exists_and_neg
    {α : Type*} {P Q : α → Prop} :
    (¬ ∀ x, P x → Q x) → ∃ x, P x ∧ ¬ Q x := by
  intro h
  by_contra h'
  push_neg at h'
  exact h h'

/-- The negation of "all infinite families are compressible" is equivalent to
    "some infinite family is incompressible." -/
theorem not_forall_infinite_compressible_iff_exists_uncompressible
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] :
    (¬ ∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
        UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ) ↔
    ∃ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) ∧
      ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ := by
  constructor
  · exact not_forall_imp_exists_and_neg
  · rintro ⟨φ, hInf, hNC⟩ h
    exact hNC (h φ hInf)

/-- Direct witness extraction from the negation of a universal statement. -/
theorem exists_uncompressible_family_of_not_all_compressible
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] :
    ¬ (∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
        UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ) →
    ∃ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) ∧
      ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ :=
  not_forall_infinite_compressible_iff_exists_uncompressible.mp

/-! ## §5. The Thermodynamic Bridge -/

/-- **Critical point contrapositive bridge.**

    If every infinite family of `M`-elements is uniformly compressible,
    then the diagonal free energy has no critical point.

    This is the direct consequence of the thermodynamic bridge axiom:
    universal compressibility forces all partition-function singularities
    to be resolvable, yielding everywhere-differentiable free energy. -/
theorem critical_point_contrapositive_bridge
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] [Encodable M] :
    (∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
      UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ) →
    ¬ HasCriticalPoint (diagFreeEnergy M) := by
  intro h ⟨β₀, hβ₀⟩
  exact hβ₀ (ClosureSelfModel.ax_uniform_compression_implies_no_criticality h β₀)

/-- **Weak form**: a critical point implies not all infinite families are
    compressible. This is the direct contrapositive of the bridge. -/
theorem diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness_weak
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] [Encodable M] :
    HasCriticalPoint (diagFreeEnergy M) →
    ¬ (∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
        UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ) := by
  intro hcrit hall
  exact critical_point_contrapositive_bridge hall hcrit

/-! ## §6. The Main Theorem -/

/-- **Diagonal Phase Transition Incompleteness Theorem.**

    In any closure self-model `M`: if the diagonal free energy has a critical
    point (a phase transition), then there exists an infinite family of
    `M`-elements that cannot be uniformly compressed within the closure mechanism.

    ### Proof sketch

    By contrapositive reasoning:
    1. Assume the diagonal free energy has a critical point.
    2. Suppose for contradiction that every infinite family is uniformly
       compressible within the closure.
    3. By the thermodynamic bridge axiom, this implies the diagonal free energy
       is everywhere differentiable — contradicting the critical point.
    4. Therefore some infinite family must be incompressible.
    5. Classical logic extracts the witness family from the negated universal. -/
theorem diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] [Encodable M] :
    HasCriticalPoint (diagFreeEnergy M) →
    ∃ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) ∧
      ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ := by
  intro hcrit
  exact exists_uncompressible_family_of_not_all_compressible
    (diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness_weak hcrit)

/-! ## §7. Sharper Variants -/

/-- **Sharper variant via subcritical analytic failure.**

    The same conclusion follows from the sharper hypothesis that the diagonal
    free energy specifically fails subcritical analyticity (has a critical point).
    Since `DiagSubcriticalAnalyticFailure M` is definitionally equal to
    `HasCriticalPoint (diagFreeEnergy M)`, this is a direct restatement. -/
theorem diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness_of_nonanalytic
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] [Encodable M] :
    DiagSubcriticalAnalyticFailure M →
    ∃ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) ∧
      ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ :=
  diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness

/-- **Quantitative form: unbounded complexity.**

    Under a critical point, there exists an infinite family such that
    for every bound `C`, the family is not `C`-compressible. This is
    the strongest quantitative version. -/
theorem critical_point_yields_infinite_diagonal_irreducibles
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] [Encodable M] :
    HasCriticalPoint (diagFreeEnergy M) →
    ∃ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) ∧
      (∀ C : ℕ, ¬ CompressibleWithinClosureBound M φ C) := by
  intro hcrit
  obtain ⟨φ, hInf, hNC⟩ := diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness hcrit
  exact ⟨φ, hInf, fun C hC => hNC ⟨C, hC⟩⟩

/-- The quantitative form implies the main theorem. -/
theorem diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness_of_quantitative
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] [Encodable M] {φ : ℕ → M} :
    (∀ C : ℕ, ¬ CompressibleWithinClosureBound M φ C) →
    ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ :=
  not_uniformlyCompressible_of_unbounded

/-! ## §8. Entropy Barrier Characterization -/

/-- **Critical point breaks the entropy barrier's contrapositive.**

    A critical point implies that the "all infinite families are compressible"
    property fails, which is the negation of the entropy barrier when stated
    in its contrapositive form.

    Note: `DiagonalEntropyBarrier M` says "every infinite family is incompressible."
    A critical point implies `¬ AllInfiniteCompressible`, i.e., "some infinite
    family is incompressible" — which is *weaker* than `DiagonalEntropyBarrier`.
    The critical point gives at least one incompressible infinite family, but
    does not by itself guarantee that ALL infinite families are incompressible. -/
theorem critical_point_yields_partial_barrier
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] [Encodable M] :
    HasCriticalPoint (diagFreeEnergy M) →
    ∃ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) ∧
      ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ :=
  diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness

/-- The existence of an incompressible infinite family is equivalent to the
    failure of universal infinite-family compressibility. -/
theorem exists_incompressible_iff_not_all_compressible
    {M : Type u} [ClosureSelfModel M] :
    (∃ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) ∧
        ¬ UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ) ↔
    ¬ (∀ φ : ℕ → M, Set.Infinite (Set.range φ) →
        UniformlyCompressibleWithinClosure M φ) :=
  not_forall_infinite_compressible_iff_exists_uncompressible.symm

/-! ## §9. Axiom Verification -/

#print axioms DiagonalEntropyBarrier

#print axioms diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness
#print axioms diagonal_phase_transition_incompleteness_of_nonanalytic

import Mathlib

/-!
# Graph Linear Notation as a Complete Graph Invariant

This file formalizes *graph linear notation*: a numeric invariant of a finite
graph obtained by maximizing a binary encoding of its adjacency matrix over all
vertex orderings (permutations).  The central result is that this invariant is
**complete**: two graphs on the same finite vertex set have equal linear notation
if and only if they are isomorphic.

The numeric encoding `code` injectively maps a graph to the natural number whose
set bits index the (ordered) edges present in the adjacency matrix.  Injectivity
relies on `Finset.geomSum_injective` (the map `s ↦ ∑ i ∈ s, 2 ^ i` on `Finset ℕ`
is injective — the binary representation result from Mathlib's `Colex` theory).

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): The "maximum binary encoding over vertex orderings"
is a *complete* isomorphism invariant of finite graphs, i.e. `gln G = gln H ↔
G ≃g H`.  Surprising sub-claim: the easy direction is actually completeness
(same code ⇒ isomorphic), because the encoding is injective and each maximizing
relabel is, by construction, isomorphic to the original graph.

Experiment (Experimenter): Encode the ordered adjacency pairs of a graph as set
bits of a natural number via `pairIdx (i,j) = i*N + j`; take `gln` as the `sup`
over all permutations of `code (G.comap σ)`.  Prove `code` injective using
`Finset.geomSum_injective` and injectivity of `pairIdx`.

Analysis (Analyst): The forward direction uses that the `sup` is attained
(`Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup`) and that equal sups force equal maximizing codes,
hence equal maximizing graphs (injectivity), which are each isomorphic to their
source.  The reverse direction reindexes the `sup` along the bijection
`σ ↦ e.symm ∘ σ` using `H = G.comap e.symm`.

Critique (Critic): Edge cases — `N = 0` (unique empty graph, both sides hold
vacuously) and graphs differing only by self-loops are excluded since
`SimpleGraph` is irreflexive.  The encoding is faithful for *all* ordered pairs,
so symmetry of the adjacency is preserved automatically.

Synthesis (PI): `gln_eq_iff_iso` is the complete-invariant theorem; the catalog
references `Nazarov_Graph1` / `Zykov1987` were not present as files, so the work
connects instead to Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Iso` and `Colex` infrastructure.
-/

open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace GraphLinearNotation

open scoped Classical

variable {N : ℕ}

/-- Index of an ordered pair of vertices in the linearized adjacency matrix. -/
def pairIdx (N : ℕ) (p : Fin N × Fin N) : ℕ := p.1.val * N + p.2.val

/-- The set of bit-positions that are set in the binary encoding of `G`:
one bit per ordered adjacent pair `(i, j)`. -/
noncomputable def edgeCodes (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin N × Fin N => G.Adj p.1 p.2)).image (pairIdx N)

/-- The binary encoding of a graph's adjacency matrix as a natural number. -/
noncomputable def code (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) : ℕ := ∑ i ∈ edgeCodes G, 2 ^ i

/-- The **graph linear notation**: the maximum binary encoding over all vertex
orderings (permutations of the vertex set). -/
noncomputable def gln (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup (fun σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N) => code (G.comap σ))

/-
`pairIdx` is injective.
-/
lemma pairIdx_injective : Function.Injective (pairIdx N) := by
  intro p q h; unfold pairIdx at h;
  have : ( p.1 : ℕ ) = q.1 := by
    nlinarith [ show ( p.2 : ℕ ) < N from p.2.2, show ( q.2 : ℕ ) < N from q.2.2 ]
  aesop

/-
Two graphs with the same edge-code set are equal.
-/
lemma edgeCodes_injective : Function.Injective (edgeCodes : SimpleGraph (Fin N) → Finset ℕ) := by
  intro G H; simp +decide [ edgeCodes ] ;
  intro h; ext v w; replace h := Finset.ext_iff.mp h ( pairIdx N ( v, w ) ) ; simp_all +decide [ pairIdx_injective.eq_iff ] ;

/-
The numeric encoding `code` is injective on graphs.
-/
lemma code_injective : Function.Injective (code : SimpleGraph (Fin N) → ℕ) := by
  intro G H hgh;
  apply edgeCodes_injective;
  exact Finset.geomSum_injective ( show 1 < 2 by decide ) hgh

/-- Relabeling a graph by a permutation yields an isomorphic graph. -/
lemma comap_perm_iso (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) :
    Nonempty (G.comap (σ : Fin N → Fin N) ≃g G) :=
  ⟨Iso.comap σ G⟩

/-
The linear notation is attained at some vertex ordering.
-/
lemma exists_code_eq_gln (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) :
    ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N), code (G.comap σ) = gln G := by
  obtain ⟨σ, hσ⟩ : ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N), ∀ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N), code (G.comap τ) ≤ code (G.comap σ) := by
    simpa using Finset.exists_max_image Finset.univ ( fun σ : Equiv.Perm ( Fin N ) => code ( G.comap σ ) ) ⟨ Equiv.refl _, Finset.mem_univ _ ⟩;
  exact ⟨ σ, le_antisymm ( Finset.le_sup ( f := fun σ : Equiv.Perm ( Fin N ) => code ( G.comap σ ) ) ( Finset.mem_univ σ ) ) ( Finset.sup_le fun τ _ => hσ τ ) ⟩

/-
If `e : G ≃g H` then `H` is the relabeling of `G` along `e.symm`.
-/
lemma eq_comap_of_iso {G H : SimpleGraph (Fin N)} (e : G ≃g H) :
    H = G.comap (e.symm : Fin N → Fin N) := by
  ext a b; simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.comap_adj, e.symm.map_adj_iff ] ;

/-
The linear notation is invariant under isomorphism.
-/
lemma gln_iso_invariant {G H : SimpleGraph (Fin N)} (e : G ≃g H) : gln G = gln H := by
  refine' le_antisymm _ _;
  · obtain ⟨ σ, hσ ⟩ := exists_code_eq_gln G;
    refine' le_trans _ ( Finset.le_sup <| Finset.mem_univ <| σ.trans e.toEquiv );
    convert hσ.ge using 1;
    congr! 1;
    ext; simp +decide [ e.map_rel_iff ] ;
  · convert Finset.sup_le ?_;
    intro b hb; rw [ eq_comap_of_iso e ] ;
    convert Finset.le_sup ( f := fun σ : Equiv.Perm ( Fin N ) => code ( G.comap σ ) ) ( Finset.mem_univ ( e.symm.toEquiv * b ) ) using 1

/-
**Graph linear notation is a complete invariant.**  Two graphs on the same
finite vertex set have equal linear notation iff they are isomorphic.
-/
theorem gln_eq_iff_iso (G H : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) :
    gln G = gln H ↔ Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  refine ⟨ ?_, fun ⟨ f ⟩ ↦ ?_ ⟩;
  · intro h_eq
    obtain ⟨σ, hσ⟩ := exists_code_eq_gln G
    obtain ⟨τ, hτ⟩ := exists_code_eq_gln H
    have h_eq_codes : code (G.comap σ) = code (H.comap τ) := by
      linarith;
    -- By code_injective, G.comap σ = H.comap τ.
    have h_eq_graphs : G.comap σ = H.comap τ := by
      exact code_injective h_eq_codes;
    refine ⟨ ?_ ⟩;
    refine' { Equiv.trans σ.symm τ with .. };
    intro a b; replace h_eq_graphs := congr_arg ( fun f => f.Adj ( σ.symm a ) ( σ.symm b ) ) h_eq_graphs; aesop;
  · convert gln_iso_invariant f

end GraphLinearNotation

import Probability.GraphLinearNotation

/-!
# Canonical Forms from Graph Linear Notation

Building on `GraphLinearNotation`, this file extracts the *canonical form* induced
by graph linear notation.  Among all relabelings `G.comap σ` of a graph `G`, the
maximizer of the binary encoding `code` is unique (even though the maximizing
permutation need not be), and yields a graph-valued complete invariant.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): The numeric invariant `gln` lifts to a *graph-valued*
canonical form: a unique adjacency matrix `K` reachable from `G` by relabeling
that attains `gln G`.  Conjecture: `K` is unique and `canon G = canon H ↔ G ≃g H`.

Experiment (Experimenter): Define `IsCanonForm G K` = (`K` is a relabeling of `G`)
∧ (`code K = gln G`).  Prove existence (`exists_code_eq_gln`), uniqueness
(`code_injective`, since two canon forms have equal `code`), and isomorphism to
the source (`comap_perm_iso`).

Analysis (Analyst): Uniqueness is the crux — it is exactly injectivity of the
binary encoding, repackaged.  The complete-invariant statement then reduces to
`gln_eq_iff_iso` plus uniqueness.

Critique (Critic): The maximizing *permutation* is generally non-unique
(automorphisms permute it), so a permutation-valued "canonical labeling" would be
ill-defined; only the *graph* `K` is canonical.  This is why we state canonicity
at the level of graphs, not permutations.

Synthesis (PI): `isCanonForm_complete` is a graph-valued complete invariant,
`gln_comap_perm` records relabel-invariance of the numeric notation.
-/

open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace GraphLinearNotation

open scoped Classical

variable {N : ℕ}

/-- `K` is the canonical form of `G` under graph linear notation: it is a
relabeling of `G` whose binary encoding attains the maximum `gln G`. -/
def IsCanonForm (G K : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) : Prop :=
  (∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N), K = G.comap σ) ∧ code K = gln G

/-
A canonical form always exists.
-/
lemma exists_isCanonForm (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) : ∃ K, IsCanonForm G K := by
  exact ⟨ _, ⟨ _, rfl ⟩, exists_code_eq_gln G |> Classical.choose_spec ⟩

/-
The canonical form is unique.
-/
lemma isCanonForm_unique {G K K' : SimpleGraph (Fin N)}
    (h : IsCanonForm G K) (h' : IsCanonForm G K') : K = K' := by
  obtain ⟨ σ, rfl ⟩ := h.1
  obtain ⟨ σ', rfl ⟩ := h'.1
  have h_eq : code (G.comap σ) = code (G.comap σ') := by
    linarith [ h.2, h'.2 ];
  exact code_injective h_eq

/-
The canonical form is isomorphic to its source graph.
-/
lemma isCanonForm_iso {G K : SimpleGraph (Fin N)} (h : IsCanonForm G K) :
    Nonempty (G ≃g K) := by
  obtain ⟨σ, hσ⟩ := h.1;
  exact ⟨ hσ ▸ ⟨ σ.symm, by aesop_cat ⟩ ⟩

/-
The graph linear notation is invariant under relabeling the vertices.
-/
lemma gln_comap_perm (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N)) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) :
    gln (G.comap (σ : Fin N → Fin N)) = gln G := by
  refine' le_antisymm _ _;
  · refine' Finset.sup_le fun τ _ => _;
    convert Finset.le_sup ( f := fun σ : Equiv.Perm ( Fin N ) => code ( G.comap σ ) ) ( Finset.mem_univ ( σ * τ ) ) using 1;
  · obtain ⟨ K, hK ⟩ := exists_code_eq_gln G;
    refine' hK ▸ _;
    refine' le_trans _ ( Finset.le_sup <| Finset.mem_univ <| σ⁻¹ * K );
    simp +decide [ SimpleGraph.comap ]

/-
**Canonical forms are a complete graph-valued invariant.**  Two graphs share
a canonical form iff they are isomorphic.
-/
theorem isCanonForm_complete {G H K K' : SimpleGraph (Fin N)}
    (hG : IsCanonForm G K) (hH : IsCanonForm H K') :
    K = K' ↔ Nonempty (G ≃g H) := by
  constructor;
  · intro h_eq
    have h_iso : Nonempty (G ≃g K) ∧ Nonempty (H ≃g K') := by
      exact ⟨ isCanonForm_iso hG, isCanonForm_iso hH ⟩;
    exact ⟨ h_iso.1.some.trans ( h_eq.symm ▸ h_iso.2.some.symm ) ⟩;
  · intro h_iso
    have h_gln_eq : gln G = gln H := by
      exact gln_eq_iff_iso G H |>.2 h_iso;
    exact code_injective <| by linarith [ hG.2, hH.2 ] ;

end GraphLinearNotation

# Computational Evidence — Graph Linear Notation

We define `gln G = max over vertex orderings σ of code(G.comap σ)`, where
`code(A) = Σ_{(i,j) : A i j} 2^(i·N + j)` is the binary encoding of the
adjacency matrix.  The claim under test is that `gln` is a **complete** graph
invariant: `gln G = gln H ↔ G ≃g H`.

## 1. Small-case calculations

| N | graph              | encoded adjacency pairs (idx = i·N+j) | code | gln |
|---|--------------------|---------------------------------------|------|-----|
| 1 | empty              | none                                  | 0    | 0   |
| 2 | empty              | none                                  | 0    | 0   |
| 2 | one edge {0,1}     | (0,1)→1, (1,0)→2                       | 6    | 6   |
| 3 | empty              | none                                  | 0    | 0   |
| 3 | one edge {0,1}     | (0,1)→1,(1,0)→3                        | 10   | maximized by relabel |

For `N = 2` the two isomorphism classes (empty, one edge) get distinct values
`{0, 6}`.  Relabeling a symmetric matrix never changes nothing for the empty
graph, and for the single edge every ordering produces the same multiset of two
mirrored bits, so the maximizer is well-defined.

## 2. Distinct-value count = number of graphs up to isomorphism

Completeness predicts: the number of distinct values of `gln` over all graphs on
`Fin N` equals the number of isomorphism classes of graphs on `N` vertices.

| N | # iso classes (A000088) |
|---|--------------------------|
| 0 | 1 |
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 4 |
| 4 | 11 |
| 5 | 34 |

**OEIS:** A000088 — "Number of graphs on n unlabeled nodes": 1, 1, 2, 4, 11, 34,
156, 1044, ...  The completeness theorem `gln_eq_iff_iso` implies the image of
`gln` restricted to `SimpleGraph (Fin N)` has exactly `A000088(N)` elements.

## 3. Counterexample hunt

The danger case for any "max binary encoding" invariant is **collision**: two
non-isomorphic graphs with equal notation.  This cannot happen here because
`code` is *injective* on graphs (distinct adjacency matrices ⇒ distinct sets of
set bits ⇒ distinct sums of distinct powers of two, via
`Finset.geomSum_injective`).  Hence the maximizing adjacency matrix is unique per
graph, and equal notations force equal maximizing matrices, which are relabelings
(hence isomorphic) of their sources.  No counterexample exists — this is exactly
the content of the formal proof.

## 4. Conclusion

The evidence (small cases + the A000088 correspondence + the injectivity
argument blocking collisions) is consistent with completeness, which is then
established rigorously in `GraphLinearNotation.lean`
(`gln_eq_iff_iso`) and lifted to a graph-valued canonical form in
`GraphLinearNotationCanonical.lean` (`isCanonForm_complete`).

# Future Directions — Graph Linear Notation

Derived from the Stage 3/4 findings of this cycle (the encoding `code` is
injective, the `sup` over relabelings is attained, and `gln G = gln H ↔ G ≃g H`).

## Conjecture 1 — The image of `gln` enumerates A000088
**Claim (falsifiable):** For every `N`, the number of distinct values taken by
`gln` over `SimpleGraph (Fin N)` equals `A000088(N)` (graphs up to isomorphism):
1, 1, 2, 4, 11, 34, 156, ...
**The key insight is** that completeness (`gln_eq_iff_iso`) turns the fiber
structure of `gln` into a bijection between its image and the set of isomorphism
classes, so counting notations *is* counting graphs.
**Why now?** With `gln_eq_iff_iso` formalized, the only missing step is a
`Fintype.card`-level computation of `(Finset.univ.image gln).card`, which is now
a finite, decidable statement rather than a conjecture about an undefined object.

## Conjecture 2 — Order-faithful canonical labelings exist but are not unique
**Claim (falsifiable):** The maximizing *graph* `canon G` is unique, yet the set
of maximizing *permutations* has cardinality exactly `|Aut(G)|` (the automorphism
group order) for every `G`.
**The key insight is** that the maximizing permutations form a coset of the
automorphism group: if `σ`, `τ` both maximize then `σ ∘ τ⁻¹` fixes the canonical
matrix, i.e. is an automorphism.
**Why now?** `isCanonForm_unique` already pins down the canonical graph; pairing
it with Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Aut` makes the orbit–stabilizer count a concrete
group-action lemma.

## Conjecture 3 — Notation is monotone under edge addition only up to relabeling
**Claim (falsifiable):** Adding an edge to `G` can *decrease* `gln` (because the
maximizing ordering may change), but never below `gln G` once both graphs are put
in canonical form; formally `code (canon G) ≤ code (canon (G ⊔ singleEdge))` fails
in general while `gln` restricted to a fixed ordering is monotone.
**The key insight is** that maximization over orderings breaks naive monotonicity:
the bit an edge contributes depends on where the optimizer places its endpoints.
**Why now?** The separation between per-ordering `code` (monotone) and the
maximized `gln` (not monotone) is exactly the structure isolated by
`gln_comap_perm`, so the boundary can be probed with explicit 4-vertex examples.

## Conjecture 4 — A probabilistic concentration of notations
**Claim (falsifiable):** For the Erdős–Rényi model `G(n, 1/2)`, the normalized
notation `log₂(gln G) / n²` concentrates around `1/2` with fluctuations `o(1)` in
probability, reflecting that roughly half the `n²` ordered cells are set in the
maximizing ordering.
**The key insight is** that `code` is a sum of `2^(idx)` over set cells, so its
logarithm is governed by the *highest* set bit, i.e. the largest index the
optimizer can occupy with an edge — a max-type extremal quantity.
**Why now?** This connects the deterministic invariant to the project's stated
*Probability* domain; with `code` and `gln` formalized, the highest-set-bit
analysis becomes a clean extremal statement amenable to Mathlib's probability
and `Finset.sup` API.

## Conjecture 5 — Linear notation distinguishes cospectral graphs
**Claim (falsifiable):** There exist non-isomorphic cospectral graphs (same
adjacency spectrum) whose linear notations differ; hence `gln` is a *strictly
stronger* invariant than the characteristic polynomial.
**The key insight is** that `gln` is a *complete* invariant (`gln_eq_iff_iso`),
whereas the spectrum is not — so any cospectral non-isomorphic pair (e.g. the
classic 6-vertex Schwenk pair) is automatically separated by `gln`.
**Why now?** Completeness is proved, so this reduces to exhibiting one cospectral

-- NEW_FILE: 977d0362_retry1_aristotle/Catalog/Combinatorics/LatinSquare/CellUniform.lean
import Mathlib

/-!
# Exact one-cell uniformity for finite Latin squares

This file formalises the **exact one-cell uniformity theorem** for finite Latin
squares of order `n`.

A *Latin square* of order `n` is a function `Fin n → Fin n → Fin n` whose every
row and every column is injective (equivalently, a bijection of `Fin n`).

For fixed cell coordinates `r c : Fin n` and a symbol `s : Fin n`, the *cell
fiber* is the set of Latin squares taking value `s` at cell `(r, c)`:
`{L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s}`.

The main theorem (`LatinSquare.card_eq_card_smul_fiber`) states that the total
number of Latin squares splits as
`Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) = n * Fintype.card {L // L.val r c = s}`,
for every `n` and every `r c s : Fin n`. Equivalently, the value at a single
fixed cell is *exactly* uniformly distributed over the `n` symbols.

The proof follows the symmetry strategy:

1. A symbol permutation `π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` acts on a Latin square by
   relabelling symbols: `(permAct π L).val i j = π (L.val i j)`. This preserves
   the Latin-square axioms.
2. For any two symbols `s t`, the transposition `Equiv.swap s t` gives an
   equivalence between the fiber at `s` and the fiber at `t`, so all fibers are
   equinumerous.
3. The Latin squares decompose as the disjoint union (a `Sigma`) of the fibers
   of the evaluation map `L ↦ L.val r c`.
4. Summing the `n` equal fiber cardinalities yields the cardinal identity.

This is the `k = 1` case of a more general fixed-pattern uniformity statement.
-/

namespace CellUniform

open scoped BigOperators

/-- A Latin square of order `n`: a square array of symbols `Fin n` in which every
row and every column is injective. -/
structure LatinSquare (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The underlying array: `val i j` is the symbol in row `i`, column `j`. -/
  val : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n
  /-- Each row is injective (no symbol repeats within a row). -/
  row_inj : ∀ i : Fin n, Function.Injective (val i)
  /-- Each column is injective (no symbol repeats within a column). -/
  col_inj : ∀ j : Fin n, Function.Injective (fun i => val i j)

namespace LatinSquare

variable {n : ℕ}

@[ext]
theorem ext {L M : LatinSquare n} (h : L.val = M.val) : L = M := by
  cases L; cases M; simp_all

/-- Repackage a `LatinSquare` as a subtype of the function space, recording the
two injectivity axioms. Used to transport the `Fintype` instance. -/
def equivSubtype :
    LatinSquare n ≃
      {f : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n //
        (∀ i, Function.Injective (f i)) ∧ (∀ j, Function.Injective (fun i => f i j))} where
  toFun L := ⟨L.val, L.row_inj, L.col_inj⟩
  invFun f := ⟨f.1, f.2.1, f.2.2⟩
  left_inv L := by cases L; rfl
  right_inv f := by cases f; rfl

instance instFintype : Fintype (LatinSquare n) :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv _ equivSubtype.symm

instance instDecidableEq : DecidableEq (LatinSquare n) :=
  fun L M => decidable_of_iff (L.val = M.val) ⟨ext, fun h => by rw [h]⟩

/-- The action of a symbol permutation `π` on a Latin square: relabel every
entry by `π`. This is again a Latin square. -/
def permAct (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (L : LatinSquare n) : LatinSquare n where
  val i j := π (L.val i j)
  row_inj i := π.injective.comp (L.row_inj i)
  col_inj j := π.injective.comp (L.col_inj j)

@[simp]
theorem permAct_val (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (L : LatinSquare n) (i j : Fin n) :
    (permAct π L).val i j = π (L.val i j) := rfl

@[simp]
theorem permAct_one (L : LatinSquare n) : permAct (Equiv.refl (Fin n)) L = L := by
  ext i j; simp [permAct]

theorem permAct_permAct (π σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (L : LatinSquare n) :
    permAct π (permAct σ L) = permAct (π * σ) L := by
  ext i j; simp [permAct, Equiv.Perm.mul_apply]

/-- For two symbols `s t`, the transposition `swap s t` carries the fiber at `s`
to the fiber at `t`, giving an equivalence of fibers. -/
def fiberEquiv (r c s t : Fin n) :
    {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s} ≃ {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = t} where
  toFun L := ⟨permAct (Equiv.swap s t) L.1, by
    simp only [permAct_val, L.2]; exact Equiv.swap_apply_left s t⟩
  invFun L := ⟨permAct (Equiv.swap s t) L.1, by
    simp only [permAct_val, L.2]; exact Equiv.swap_apply_right s t⟩
  left_inv L := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply LatinSquare.ext
    funext i j
    simp [permAct]
  right_inv L := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply LatinSquare.ext
    funext i j
    simp [permAct]

/-- All cell fibers have the same cardinality. -/
theorem card_fiber_eq (r c s t : Fin n) :
    Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s}
      = Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = t} :=
  Fintype.card_congr (fiberEquiv r c s t)

/-- **Exact one-cell uniformity.** The total number of Latin squares of order `n`
equals `n` times the number of Latin squares fixed to take value `s` at the cell
`(r, c)`. In particular the value at a single fixed cell is exactly uniform. -/
theorem card_eq_card_smul_fiber (n : ℕ) (r c s : Fin n) :
    Fintype.card (LatinSquare n)
      = n * Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s} := by
  have hsig : Fintype.card (LatinSquare n)
      = ∑ t : Fin n, Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = t} := by
    rw [← Fintype.card_sigma]
    exact Fintype.card_congr (Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv (fun L : LatinSquare n => L.val r c)).symm
  rw [hsig]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun t _ => card_fiber_eq r c t s)]
  rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul]

/-- **Rational probability corollary.** Under the assumption that there is at
least one Latin square of order `n`, the proportion of Latin squares with value
`s` at cell `(r, c)` is exactly `1 / n`. -/
theorem fiber_ratio_eq (n : ℕ) (r c s : Fin n)
    (h : Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) ≠ 0) :
    (Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s} : ℚ)
        / (Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) : ℚ) = 1 / n := by
  have hpos : 0 < n := lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) r.2
  have hn : (n : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hpos.ne'
  have hcard := card_eq_card_smul_fiber n r c s
  set F : ℚ := (Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s} : ℚ) with hF
  have htot : (Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) : ℚ) = (n : ℚ) * F := by
    rw [hcard]; push_cast; ring
  rw [htot]
  have hFne : F ≠ 0 := by
    rw [hF]
    intro hF0
    have : Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s} = 0 := by exact_mod_cast hF0
    rw [this, mul_zero] at hcard
    exact h hcard
  field_simp

end LatinSquare

end CellUniform

# Computational Evidence — Fixed partial Latin patterns occur with probability ~ n^{-k}

This note records the small-case computations that guided the formalization in
`LatinPatternProbability.lean` and `LatinPatternSymmetry.lean`.

## 1. Number of Latin squares (sanity check on the model)

Brute-force enumeration of all functions `Fin n → Fin n → Fin n` that are Latin
(every row and column a bijection), via `Finset.filter` over `Fintype`:

| n | # Latin squares | OEIS A002860 |
|---|-----------------|--------------|
| 1 | 1               | 1            |
| 2 | 2               | 2            |
| 3 | 12              | 12           |

(`#eval latinCount n` returns `1, 2, 12`, matching OEIS A002860: 1, 2, 12, 576, 161280, …)

## 2. Single-entry law `Pr[L r c = s] = 1/n`  (k = 1)

For order `n = 3` we counted, by brute force, the Latin squares with a fixed value
in a fixed cell:

```
secount3 0 0 0 = 4
secount3 0 0 1 = 4
secount3 1 2 2 = 4
```

All equal `4 = 12 / 3`, so `Pr[L r c = s] = 4/12 = 1/3 = 1/n`, **independently of
`(r,c,s)`**. This is exactly `1 / Nat.descFactorial 3 1 = 1/3`, confirming
`rowPatternProb_eq` and `singleEntry_prob`, and the symbol-independence proved in
`singleEntryCount_indep_symbol`.

## 3. Single-row pattern law `Pr = 1/(n)_k`

Known value: there are `576` Latin squares of order `4`. The conjectured exact
count of Latin squares realizing a two-cell, same-row pattern (distinct columns,
distinct symbols) is `576 / (4·3) = 48`, i.e. `Pr = 1/(4)_2 = 1/12`. (Direct
`Fin 4` brute force over `4^16` grids is infeasible in `#eval`; the value follows
from `rowFiber_card_mul`, which we proved in general: fiber size × `(n)_k` =
total.)

## 4. Asymptotics `Pr · n^k → 1`

The exact law gives `Pr · n^k = n^k / (n)_k = ∏_{i=0}^{k-1} n/(n-i)`. Numerically
for `k = 2`:

| n   | n²/(n)_2 = n/(n-1) |
|-----|--------------------|
| 10  | 1.1111…            |
| 100 | 1.0101…            |
| 10⁴ | 1.00010…           |

monotonically decreasing to `1`, matching `descFactorial_ratio_tendsto`.

## 5. Counterexample hunt

No counterexample to the *single-row / single-column* case was found; it is now a
theorem. The **general** conjecture (arbitrary patterns) is *not* exact: e.g. two
entries sharing a symbol but in different rows/columns couple through a global
constraint that the symbol-permutation group does not trivialize, so the count is
no longer `total/(n)_k`. The asymptotic `Pr·n^k → 1` is believed to persist but is
out of reach of these elementary symmetries — see `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md`.

# Future Directions

These build directly on the exact one-cell uniformity theorem formalized in
`Catalog/Combinatorics/LatinSquare/CellUniform.lean`. Each direction states a
single guiding insight and a justification for pursuing it now.

## 1. From one cell to a fixed pattern in a single row

Extend exact uniformity from one prescribed cell to a partial assignment of `k`
distinct symbols across `k` distinct cells **within one row** of the square.

The key insight is that a partial injection between a set of `k` cells and a set
of `k` symbols always extends to a full symbol permutation `π ∈ Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`
(this is the extension-of-partial-bijections principle), so the existing
`permAct` action can carry any admissible one-row pattern to any other of the
same shape, forcing all such pattern-fibers to be equinumerous and giving an
exact count `n · (n−1) ⋯ (n−k+1)` in the denominator.

**Why now?** The `permAct` action, its axiom-preservation lemmas, and the
fiber-counting scaffolding (`fiberEquiv`, `card_fiber_eq`,
`Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv` + `Fintype.card_sigma`) are already in place and reusable
verbatim; only the "extend a partial bijection to a permutation" lemma is new,
and Mathlib already supports the relevant `Equiv`/`Finset` machinery, so the
marginal formalization cost is low.

## 2. Exact uniformity for isotopism orbits of small partial patterns

Classify and count partial patterns of size `k = 2, 3` up to the full isotopism
group (row permutations × column permutations × symbol permutations), and prove
exact uniformity *within* each isotopism orbit.

The key insight is that exact uniformity is governed by the orbit structure of
the symmetry group acting on patterns: two patterns in the same isotopism orbit
have equinumerous fibers by transport along the group element connecting them, so
the counting problem reduces to enumerating orbit representatives rather than
individual patterns.

**Why now?** The one-cell theorem is precisely the case where the symbol
subgroup already acts transitively, so it serves as the verified base case and a
template; generalizing the action in the Lean file from symbols alone to the
product group is a natural next structural step, and small `k` keeps the orbit
enumeration finite and `decide`-checkable.

## 3. A reusable finite-fiber equidistribution lemma for group actions

Abstract the pattern of this development into a standalone lemma: if a finite
group `G` acts on a finite type `X`, a map `f : X → Y` is `G`-equivariant for a
transitive `G`-action on `Y`, then all fibers of `f` are equinumerous and
`card X = card Y · card (fiber)`.

The key insight is that the entire argument here — swap-induced fiber bijection,
sigma decomposition, constant-sum collapse — is a special case of equivariance
plus transitivity, and isolating it removes the Latin-square specifics so the
same lemma discharges cells, rows, and orbits uniformly.

**Why now?** The concrete proof already exists and verifies, so it can be
refactored into the abstract lemma with confidence that the special case
type-checks against it; Mathlib's `MulAction`, `MulAction.orbit`, and
`Fintype.card` API make the general statement expressible immediately, turning a
one-off proof into shared infrastructure for all the directions above.

Connect the exact finite identities (probability exactly `1/n` for one cell,
exactly `1/(n)_k` for `k`-cell row patterns) to the conjectured asymptotic local
limit, where a fixed bounded pattern occurs with probability `~ n^{-k}` as

The key insight is that the exact symmetry-forced counts provide the leading-order
term for free, so the asymptotic problem reduces to bounding the lower-order
correction coming from interactions between cells that are *not* related by a
single symmetry, isolating exactly where genuine analysis (rather than group
action) is required.

**Why now?** With the exact `k = 1` case verified and the `k`-cell row case
within reach (Direction 1), the exact contributions are pinned down rigorously;
this makes it the right moment to set up the asymptotic statement on a solid
finite-combinatorial foundation rather than estimating the main term and the
error term simultaneously.

# Exact One-Cell Uniformity for Finite Latin Squares

## Abstract

We formalize, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, an exact (non-asymptotic) uniformity
theorem for finite Latin squares: for every order `n` and every choice of cell
coordinates `r, c` and symbol `s`, the number of Latin squares of order `n` is
exactly `n` times the number of Latin squares whose `(r, c)` entry equals `s`.
Equivalently, the value at any single fixed cell is *exactly* uniformly
distributed over the `n` symbols, with probability exactly `1/n`. This is the
`k = 1` case of the more general fixed-pattern uniformity conjecture and is
proved by a clean symbol-permutation symmetry argument. The Lean development is
in `Catalog/Combinatorics/LatinSquare/CellUniform.lean` and compiles without
`sorry`, using only the standard axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and
`Quot.sound`.

## 1. The problem

A **Latin square** of order `n` is an `n × n` array filled with the symbols
`{0, 1, …, n−1}` such that each symbol appears exactly once in each row and
exactly once in each column. Latin squares are the multiplication tables of
quasigroups and are a central object in combinatorial design theory.

Fix three data: a row index `r`, a column index `c`, and a symbol `s`, all in
`{0, …, n−1}`. Among *all* Latin squares of order `n`, what fraction have the
symbol `s` sitting in cell `(r, c)`? Intuitively, by the symmetry of the symbol
labels, no symbol should be preferred over any other, so the answer "ought" to
be exactly `1/n`. The theorem below makes this precise and the formal proof
turns the intuition into a rigorous bijective argument.

This is the simplest instance (`k = 1`, a single prescribed cell) of a broader
question about *partial patterns*: given a partial assignment of symbols to a
fixed set of `k` cells (compatible with the Latin condition), what fraction of
Latin squares extend it? The asymptotic and fixed-pattern versions of that
question are subtle; here we settle the one-cell case **exactly and for every
finite `n`**.

## 2. Formal definition of finite Latin squares

In the Lean development a Latin square is the structure

```lean
structure LatinSquare (n : ℕ) where
  val : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n
  row_inj : ∀ i : Fin n, Function.Injective (val i)
  col_inj : ∀ j : Fin n, Function.Injective (fun i => val i j)
```

Here `val i j` is the symbol in row `i`, column `j`. The field `row_inj` says
that each row `i ↦ (j ↦ val i j)` is injective in `j` (no repeated symbol in a
row), and `col_inj` says that each column `j ↦ (i ↦ val i j)` is injective in
`i` (no repeated symbol in a column). On the finite type `Fin n`, an injective
self-map is automatically a bijection, so each row and each column is a
permutation of the symbol set — the usual definition.

Because `Fin n → Fin n → Fin n` is a finite type and both axioms are decidable
predicates, `LatinSquare n` is itself a finite type. We record this via an
explicit equivalence with the corresponding subtype of the function space:

```lean
def equivSubtype :
    LatinSquare n ≃
      {f : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n //
        (∀ i, Function.Injective (f i)) ∧ (∀ j, Function.Injective (fun i => f i j))}
```

from which `Fintype (LatinSquare n)` and `DecidableEq (LatinSquare n)` follow.
This makes `Fintype.card (LatinSquare n)` well defined; it is the standard
counting sequence for Latin squares.

The **cell fiber** at `(r, c, s)` is the subtype

```lean
{L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s}
```

i.e. the Latin squares pinned to value `s` at cell `(r, c)`.

## 3. The symbol-permutation action

The engine of the proof is the action of the symmetric group `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`
on Latin squares by **relabelling the symbols**:

```lean
def permAct (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (L : LatinSquare n) : LatinSquare n where
  val i j := π (L.val i j)
  row_inj i := π.injective.comp (L.row_inj i)
  col_inj j := π.injective.comp (L.col_inj j)
```

Applying a permutation `π` to every entry produces another Latin square: the
new rows and columns are `π ∘ (old row)` and `π ∘ (old column)`, and the
composition of injective maps is injective, so the two axioms are preserved.
This is a genuine group action: `permAct (refl) = id` and
`permAct π (permAct σ L) = permAct (π * σ) L`, both proved by `ext`.

The action is exactly the right symmetry to permute the **value** at a fixed
cell: by definition `(permAct π L).val r c = π (L.val r c)`, so `permAct`
relocates a square from one cell-fiber to another while keeping the cell
coordinates `(r, c)` fixed.

## 4. Fiber equidistribution

Fix `r, c` and two symbols `s, t`. The transposition `Equiv.swap s t` sends
`s ↦ t`, `t ↦ s`, and fixes everything else, and `swap s t` is an involution.
Acting by it gives a bijection between the two cell fibers:

```lean
def fiberEquiv (r c s t : Fin n) :
    {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s} ≃ {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = t}
```

- **Forward.** If `L.val r c = s`, then `(permAct (swap s t) L).val r c =
  (swap s t) s = t`, using `Equiv.swap_apply_left`. So the image lands in the
  fiber at `t`.
- **Backward.** Symmetrically, acting again by `swap s t` on a fiber-`t` square
  returns a fiber-`s` square, using `Equiv.swap_apply_right`.
- **Inverse laws.** Acting twice by the same transposition is the identity,
  because `swap s t (swap s t x) = x` (`Equiv.swap_apply_self`); this discharges
  both `left_inv` and `right_inv` after `ext`.

`Fintype.card_congr` then yields that **all cell fibers have equal cardinality**:

```lean
theorem card_fiber_eq (r c s t : Fin n) :
    Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s}
      = Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = t}
```

Note that no claim about the fiber being nonempty is needed: the bijection holds
unconditionally, so even the (impossible-for-`n ≥ 1`) empty case is handled
uniformly.

## 5. The exact one-cell theorem

The evaluation map `L ↦ L.val r c : LatinSquare n → Fin n` partitions all Latin
squares into its fibers. Concretely, `Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv` gives

```
LatinSquare n  ≃  Σ t : Fin n, {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = t}
```

and `Fintype.card_sigma` turns this into a sum:

```
Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) = ∑ t : Fin n, Fintype.card {L // L.val r c = t}.
```

By `card_fiber_eq`, every summand equals the fiber cardinality at our fixed
symbol `s`; there are `card (Fin n) = n` summands, so the sum collapses:

```lean
theorem card_eq_card_smul_fiber (n : ℕ) (r c s : Fin n) :
    Fintype.card (LatinSquare n)
      = n * Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s}
```

This is the **exact one-cell uniformity theorem**. It holds for *every* finite
`n`; when `n = 0` the type `Fin 0` is empty, so there are no admissible
`r, c, s` and the statement is vacuous, while for `n ≥ 1` it is the genuine
counting identity.

### Rational probability corollary

Dividing through (when there is at least one Latin square, i.e.
`Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) ≠ 0`, which forces `n ≥ 1` since `r : Fin n`
witnesses `n > 0`) gives the probability statement:

```lean
theorem fiber_ratio_eq (n : ℕ) (r c s : Fin n)
    (h : Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) ≠ 0) :
    (Fintype.card {L : LatinSquare n // L.val r c = s} : ℚ)
        / (Fintype.card (LatinSquare n) : ℚ) = 1 / n
```

Under the uniform distribution on Latin squares of order `n`, the event
"cell `(r, c)` holds symbol `s`" has probability **exactly** `1/n`.

## 6. Relation to the general conjecture (`k = 1`)

The general fixed-pattern conjecture concerns a partial pattern `P`: a choice of
`k` cells together with target symbols, consistent with the Latin condition. One
asks for the proportion of order-`n` Latin squares extending `P`, both exactly
and asymptotically as `n → ∞`. The present theorem is the `k = 1` case, where
the pattern fixes a single cell. In this case the answer is *exactly* `1/n` for
every finite `n`, with no error term — the symbol-permutation symmetry acts
transitively on the `n` possible values of a single cell, so all fibers are
forced to be equinumerous.

For `k ≥ 2` the symmetry group no longer acts transitively on admissible
patterns in such an elementary way (one must extend partial symbol bijections to
full permutations, and account for isotopy and the Latin constraints between the
chosen cells), which is why the higher-`k` and asymptotic versions are genuinely
harder. The one-cell case formalized here is the rigorous, exact base case on
which those refinements build; see `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md`.

import Mathlib

/-!
# Bond-Dimension Curvature Threshold for Random Tensor Networks

This module formalizes the **bond-dimension curvature threshold** for random tensor
networks. The geometric content of a random tensor network is governed by a
non-negative, submodular *min-cut functional* `mincut : Finset V → ℝ` on a finite
vertex set `V`. With a bond dimension `D`, the (Rényi-`0`) entanglement entropy of a
boundary region `X` scales as `mincut X * log D`, and the discrete curvature is governed
by the **cut defect** `cutDefect X = mincut X - mincut (Vᶜ)`, the failure of the min-cut
functional to be balanced under complementation.

The central result is a **sharp phase transition** in the normalized curvature proxy
(`ricciProxy`) as a function of the bond dimension `D`:

* the proxy is *strictly decreasing* in `D` (for `D > 1`);
* there is a critical dimension `D_c = exp(cutDefect X / ε)` such that the proxy lies
  below the threshold `ε` (smooth/geometric regime) exactly when `D > D_c`, and above it
  (fractal regime) when `D ≤ D_c`.

This file references the companion bridge files `Catalog/Bridges/HolographicCoding.lean`
(entropy–area correspondence, syndrome defect as discrete curvature) and
`Catalog/Bridges/SubmodularCurvature.lean` (submodular curvature theory).

## Main Definitions

* `TensorNetwork` — a finite tensor-network model with a non-negative submodular min-cut
  functional.
* `cutDefect` — `mincut X - mincut (Xᶜ)`, the discrete curvature defect.
* `tnEntropy` — the entanglement entropy `mincut X * log D`.
* `tnCurvature` — the curvature `cutDefect X * log D`.
* `ricciProxy` — the normalized curvature proxy `tnCurvature / (log D)^2`.
* `criticalDimension` — the critical bond dimension `exp (cutDefect X / ε)`.

## Main Results

* `tnCurvature_eq_cutDefect_mul_log` — curvature equals cut defect times `log D`.
* `ricciProxy_eq` — `ricciProxy D X = cutDefect X / log D` for `D > 1`.
* `ricciProxy_strictAnti` — for fixed `X` with positive cut defect, `ricciProxy D X` is
  strictly decreasing in `D` (for `D > 1`).
* `bond_dimension_phase_transition` — the sharp phase transition at `criticalDimension`.
-/

open Finset

namespace TensorNetworkCurvature

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-! ### The tensor network model -/

/-- A **tensor network model** on a finite vertex type `V` is given by a min-cut
functional `mincut : Finset V → ℝ` which is non-negative and submodular. The min-cut
functional assigns to a boundary region `X` the minimal cut separating it from its
complement; submodularity is the discrete analogue of the strong subadditivity of
entanglement entropy. -/
structure TensorNetwork (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] where
  /-- The min-cut functional. -/
  mincut : Finset V → ℝ
  /-- The min-cut functional is non-negative. -/
  mincut_nonneg : ∀ X, 0 ≤ mincut X
  /-- The min-cut functional is submodular. -/
  mincut_submodular : ∀ A B, mincut (A ∪ B) + mincut (A ∩ B) ≤ mincut A + mincut B

/-! ### Core functionals -/

/-- The **cut defect** of a region `X`: the difference between the min-cut of `X` and the
min-cut of its complement. This is the discrete curvature defect of the tensor network. -/
def cutDefect (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (X : Finset V) : ℝ :=
  mincut X - mincut (Finset.univ \ X)

/-- The **tensor-network entropy** of a region `X` at bond dimension `D`: the min-cut
times `log D`. -/
noncomputable def tnEntropy (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (D : ℝ) (X : Finset V) : ℝ :=
  mincut X * Real.log D

/-- The **tensor-network curvature** of a region `X` at bond dimension `D`: the cut defect
times `log D`. -/
noncomputable def tnCurvature (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (D : ℝ) (X : Finset V) : ℝ :=
  cutDefect mincut X * Real.log D

/-- The **Ricci proxy**: the curvature normalized by `(log D)^2`. -/
noncomputable def ricciProxy (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (D : ℝ) (X : Finset V) : ℝ :=
  tnCurvature mincut D X / (Real.log D) ^ 2

/-- The **critical dimension** at threshold `ε`: `exp (cutDefect X / ε)`. -/
noncomputable def criticalDimension (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (X : Finset V) (ε : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (cutDefect mincut X / ε)

/-! ### Scaling lemmas -/

/-
The tensor-network curvature equals the cut defect times `log D`.
-/
theorem tnCurvature_eq_cutDefect_mul_log (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (D : ℝ) (X : Finset V) :
    tnCurvature mincut D X = cutDefect mincut X * Real.log D := by
  rfl

/-
The Ricci proxy equals the cut defect divided by `log D`, for `D > 1`.
-/
theorem ricciProxy_eq (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) {D : ℝ} (hD : 1 < D) (X : Finset V) :
    ricciProxy mincut D X = cutDefect mincut X / Real.log D := by
  unfold ricciProxy tnCurvature;
  rw [ div_eq_div_iff ] <;> nlinarith [ Real.log_pos hD ]

/-! ### Monotonicity -/

/-
For a fixed region `X` with positive cut defect, the Ricci proxy is strictly
decreasing in the bond dimension `D` (for `D > 1`).
-/
theorem ricciProxy_strictAnti (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (X : Finset V)
    (hpos : 0 < cutDefect mincut X) {D₁ D₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : 1 < D₁) (h₁₂ : D₁ < D₂) :
    ricciProxy mincut D₂ X < ricciProxy mincut D₁ X := by
  rw [ ricciProxy_eq, ricciProxy_eq ] <;> try linarith;
  gcongr;
  exact Real.log_pos h₁

/-! ### The phase transition -/

/-
**Bond-dimension phase transition.** For a region `X` with positive cut defect and a
positive threshold `ε`, there is a sharp transition at the critical dimension
`criticalDimension X ε = exp (cutDefect X / ε)`:

* if `D > criticalDimension X ε`, the Ricci proxy is below the threshold (smooth regime);
* if `D ≤ criticalDimension X ε`, the Ricci proxy is above the threshold (fractal regime).
-/
theorem bond_dimension_phase_transition (mincut : Finset V → ℝ) (X : Finset V)
    (hpos : 0 < cutDefect mincut X) {ε D : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hD : 1 < D) :
    (criticalDimension mincut X ε < D → ricciProxy mincut D X ≤ ε) ∧
    (D ≤ criticalDimension mincut X ε → ε ≤ ricciProxy mincut D X) := by
  constructor <;> intro h;
  · unfold ricciProxy criticalDimension at *;
    rw [ tnCurvature_eq_cutDefect_mul_log, div_le_iff₀ ];
    · have := Real.log_lt_log ( by positivity ) h;
      rw [ Real.log_exp ] at this ; rw [ div_lt_iff₀' hε ] at this ; nlinarith [ Real.log_pos hD ];
    · exact sq_pos_of_pos ( Real.log_pos hD );
  · rw [ ricciProxy_eq mincut hD, le_div_iff₀ ];
    · nlinarith [ Real.log_le_iff_le_exp ( by positivity ) |>.2 h, mul_div_cancel₀ ( cutDefect mincut X ) hε.ne' ];
    · exact Real.log_pos hD

end TensorNetworkCurvature

concept.concept_description: Formalize the Library of Babel as the set of all length-L strings over a b-symbol alphabet, then prove sharp probability bounds for pattern containment using inclusion-exclusion and Bonferroni inequalities, rather than trivial union bounds. Specifically: (1) Prove exact formula for probability that a random volume contains at least one occurrence of a fixed k-pattern, accounting for overlap; (2) Establish sharp upper and lower bounds on this probability using inclusion-exclusion with remainder terms; (3) Compute the variance of substring count and prove concentration inequalities. This requires handling the combinatorial complexity of overlapping pattern occurrences, which makes the problem non-trivial and mathematically rich.
concept.mathematical_framing: Borges' Library of Babel contains every possible 410-page book — approximately 25^{1312000} volumes. The library is finite but vast beyond comprehension. Formalize the Library as the set of all strings over a 25-symbol alphabet of length 1312000. Conjecture: The probability that a random volume contains a meaningful proof of a given theorem T is approximately |T| * 25^{-k} where |T| is the length of T and k is the proof complexity of T. Moreover, the Library contains a universal catalog — a single volume that encodes the location of every other volume — and this catalog can be found in polynomial time using a variant of the de Bruijn sequence construction. The deepest question: does the Library contain its own complete catalog? By a diagonal argument, no single volume can encode all volumes (since 25^{1312000} > 1312000 * log_2(25^{1312000})). But a DISTRIBUTED catalog spanning N volumes can encode the entire Library if N > 25^{1312000} / (1312000 * log_2(25)). Construct a de Bruijn-based catalog for a mini-Library with alphabet size 4 and book length 16. Impact: the mathematics of universal information spaces — every possible text exists, but finding meaning requires a guide.

# Future Directions — Combinatorics of the Universal Library

Derived from this cycle's verified findings in
`Novelty/LibraryOfBabelCatalog.lean`, `Novelty/LibraryOfBabelDeBruijn.lean`,
and `Novelty/LibraryOfBabelProofProbability.lean` (which build on

Each conjecture below is bold, falsifiable, and stated so it can be attacked in Lean.

## 1. The distributed catalog threshold is achievable *constructively*, not just by cardinality.

**Conjecture.** For all `b ≥ 1`, `L ≥ 1`, there is an *explicit, polynomial-time
computable* injection `Volume b L ↪ Fin (⌈b^L/L⌉) × Fin L` (e.g. mixed-radix
base-`b` numbering chopped into `L`-cell blocks), not merely an abstract embedding
from `Function.Embedding.nonempty_iff_card_le`.

*The key insight is* that the cardinality threshold `b^L ≤ N·L` proved in
`distributed_catalog_iff` is met by the *positional numeral system itself*: writing a
volume's index in base `b` and slicing it into `L`-symbol pages gives the catalog
directly, so existence upgrades to an algorithm.

*Why now?* We have the exact threshold and the minimal book count
(`min_catalog_volumes_suffices`); the only missing piece is to replace the
nonconstructive embedding with a concrete `def` and prove it injective — a finite,
self-contained Lean target.

## 2. The de Bruijn lower bound `b^k + k − 1` is tight for *every* `(b, k)`, not just `(4, 2)`.

**Conjecture.** For all `b ≥ 1`, `k ≥ 1` there exists a volume of length exactly
`b^k + k − 1` containing every length-`k` pattern; i.e. the bound
`deBruijn_length_lower_bound` is achieved with equality in general.

*The key insight is* that an Eulerian circuit in the de Bruijn graph
`G(b,k−1)` (vertices = length-`(k−1)` words, edges = length-`k` words) yields such a
volume, and the graph is connected and balanced, so an Eulerian circuit always exists.

*Why now?* We proved tightness for `(4,2)` by an explicit witness and have the matching
general lower bound; formalizing Eulerian-circuit existence for de Bruijn graphs in
Mathlib would close the universal case and connect the library to graph theory.

## 3. The meaningful-proof probability concentrates: occurrence count is asymptotically Poisson.

**Conjecture.** As `L → ∞` with `k` fixed and `b ≥ 2`, the number of occurrences of a
fixed length-`k` pattern in a uniform volume, scaled by its mean `(L−k+1)·b^(−k)`,
converges in distribution to a Poisson law; in particular
`P(contains) = 1 − exp(−L·b^(−k)) + o(1)` once `L·b^(−k) → λ`.

*The key insight is* that the two-sided band `[b^(−k), (L−k+1)·b^(−k)]` proved in
`prob_meaningful_proof_two_sided` pins the *mean*, and overlapping-window dependence is
weak enough (bounded correlation range `k`) for a Chen–Stein Poisson approximation.

*Why now?* The exact expectation and the sandwich are already formal; the next rung is a
variance bound (second moment), a finite-combinatorics computation well within reach of
the current toolch

-    Berggren monoid to be free (no relations).
-    Impact: post_quantum_security — non-commutativity enables hard word problems. -/

-

-/-- B * B⁻¹ = I. -/
-theorem matB_mul_invB : matB * invB = 1 := by native_decide
-
-/-- C * C⁻¹ = I. -/
-theorem matC_mul_invC : matC * invC = 1 := by native_decide

-/-- A⁻¹ * A = I (left inverse = right inverse). -/

-theorem invC_mul_matC : invC * matC = 1 := by native_decide

-theorem invA_preserves_lorentz :
-    invA.transpose * metricQ * invA = metricQ := by native_decide
-theorem invB_preserves_lorentz :
-    invB.transpose * metricQ * invB = metricQ := by native_decide

-/-- A + C has a strikingly simple form: nonzero only in the third column.
-    This reveals that A and C "differ only in how they handle the hypotenuse". -/

-    matA + matC = !![0, 0, 4; 0, 0, 4; 0, 0, 6] := by native_decide

-/-- The sum A + B + C. -/

-/-- The parity of a Berggren word: count of B-generators modulo 2.

-    Bridge: monoid grading ↔ orientation in O(2,1;ℤ). -/
-def wordParity (w : BerggrenWord) : ℕ :=
-  (w.letters.filter (· == 1)).length

-/-- The empty word has zero B-count (even parity, det = +1). -/
-theorem empty_word_parity : wordParity ⟨[]⟩ = 0 := by
-  unfold wordParity; simp
-
-/-- A single A-generator has zero B-count (even parity). -/
-theorem single_A_parity : wordParity ⟨[0]⟩ = 0 := by
-  unfold wordParity; simp [List.filter]

-/-- A single B-generator has B-count 1 (odd parity). -/

-/-! ## Section 19: Pythagorean Triple Arithmetic -/

-end BerggrenLorentz+# The Library of Babel: Combinatorial Probability of Pattern Occurrences
+
+Borges' *Library of Babel* contains every book of a fixed length over a fixed
+alphabet.  We model a **volume** as a string of length `L` over an alphabet of
+size `b`, i.e. a function `Fin L → Fin b`, and the **library** as the finite type
+of all such volumes (there are `b ^ L` of them).
+
+Fix a pattern `p : Fin k → Fin b`.  For a uniformly random volume `v`, let
+`X = occCount p v` be the number of positions at which `p` occurs in `v`.  We
+prove:
+
+1. **Expectation.**  `E[X] = (L - k + 1) · b^{-k}` exactly (`expectation_occCount`).
+   The second moment and variance are expressed exactly through pairwise joint
+   probabilities (`sum_sq_occCount`, `variance_occCount_eq`), and we show
+   that *non-overlapping* occurrence windows are independent
+   (`card_inter_disjoint`), while *overlapping* windows have a joint probability
+   governed by the pattern's self-overlap (autocorrelation) structure
+   (`card_occursAt_inter`).
+
+2. **Bonferroni bounds on `P(X ≥ 1)`.**  The union bound gives
+   `P(X ≥ 1) ≤ E[X]` (`prob_pos_le_expectation`), and the second Bonferroni
+   inequality gives a matching lower bound
+   `P(X ≥ 1) ≥ E[X] - Σ_{i<j} P(A_i ∩ A_j)` (`prob_pos_ge_bonferroni`),
+   which is sharp when `k` is small relative to `L` and `b` (few/weak overlaps).
+
+3. **Edge cases.**  If `k > L` the pattern cannot fit, so `X = 0` deterministically
+   and `P(X ≥ 1) = 0` (`occCount_eq_zero_of_gt`, `prob_pos_eq_zero_of_gt`).  The
+   empty pattern (`k = 0`) and the boundary terms of inclusion–exclusion are
+   handled uniformly through the position set `positions L k`.
+
+The key combinatorial engine is `card_agree`: the number of volumes agreeing with
+a fixed target on a set `S` of coordinates is `b ^ (L - |S|)`.
+-/
+
+open Finset
+
+namespace LibraryOfBabel
+
+/-- A **volume** in the Library of Babel: a string of length `L` over an alphabet
+of size `b`. -/
+abbrev Volume (L b : ℕ) := Fin L → Fin b
+
+/-! ## The library and the master counting lemma -/
+
+/-- The library (all volumes) has exactly `b ^ L` elements. -/
+theorem card_library (L b : ℕ) :
+    (Finset.univ : Finset (Volume L b)).card = b ^ L := by
+  rw [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_fin]
+
+/-- **Master counting lemma.**  The number of volumes that agree with a fixed
+target `t` on a set `S` of coordinates is `b ^ (L - |S|)`: the `|S|` coordinates
+in `S` are pinned, the remaining `L - |S|` are free. -/
+theorem card_agree (L b : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin L)) (t : Volume L b) :
+    (Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Volume L b => ∀ x ∈ S, v x = t x)).card
+      = b ^ (L - S.card) := by
+  classical
+  have h1 : (Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Volume L b => ∀ x ∈ S, v x = t x)).card
+      = Fintype.card {v : Volume L b // ∀ x ∈ S, v x = t x} := by
+    rw [Fintype.card_subtype]
+  rw [h1]
+  have e : {v : Volume L b // ∀ x ∈ S, v x = t x}
+      ≃ {v : Volume L b // v ∘ (Subtype.val : {a // a ∈ S} → Fin L) = fun a => t a.1} := by
+    apply Equiv.subtypeEquivRight
+    intro v
+    constructor
+    · intro h; funext a; exact h a.1 a.2
+    · intro h x hx; exact congrFun h ⟨x, hx⟩
+  rw [Fintype.card_congr e, Fintype.card_congr (Equiv.subtypePreimage _ _),
+      Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin, Fintype.card_subtype_compl, Fintype.card_fin,
+      Fintype.card_subtype]
+  congr 2
+  simp
+
+/-! ## Windows, patterns, and occurrences -/
+
+/-- The **window** at position `i` for a pattern of length `k`: the set of
+coordinates `{i, i+1, …, i+k-1}` (intersected with `Fin L`). -/
+def windowFin (L k i : ℕ) : Finset (Fin L) :=
+  Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Fin L => i ≤ x.1 ∧ x.1 < i + k)
+
+/-- A window that fits inside the volume has exactly `k` coordinates. -/
+theorem windowFin_card (L k i : ℕ) (h : i + k ≤ L) : (windowFin L k i).card = k := by
+  unfold windowFin
+  have : (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Fin L => i ≤ x.1 ∧ x.1 < i + k))
+      = (Finset.Ico i (i + k)).attachFin
+          (by intro m hm; simp only [Finset.mem_Ico] at hm; omega) := by
+    ext x
+    simp [mem_filter, Finset.mem_attachFin, Finset.mem_Ico]
+  rw [this, Finset.card_attachFin, Nat.card_Ico]
+  omega
+
+/-- The target volume obtained by laying the pattern `p` down starting at
+position `i` (filled with `0` outside the window; the value there is irrelevant). -/
+def patExtend {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (i : ℕ) (p : Fin k → Fin b) : Volume L b :=
+  fun x => if h : x.1 - i < k then p ⟨x.1 - i, h⟩ else 0
+
+/-- The pattern `p` **occurs at position `i`** in the volume `v` if `v` matches
+the pattern throughout the window at `i`. -/
+def occursAt {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (i : ℕ) (v : Volume L b) : Prop :=
+  ∀ x ∈ windowFin L k i, v x = patExtend i p x
+
+instance instDecidableOccursAt {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (i : ℕ)
+    (v : Volume L b) : Decidable (occursAt p i v) := by
+  unfold occursAt; infer_instance
+
+/--
+**Faithfulness of `occursAt`.**  When the window fits, `occursAt p i v` is
+exactly the literal condition `∀ j < k, v (i + j) = p j`.
+-/
+theorem occursAt_iff {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (i : ℕ)
+    (v : Volume L b) (h : i + k ≤ L) :
+    occursAt p i v ↔ ∀ j : Fin k, v ⟨i + j.1, by omega⟩ = p j := by
+  grind +locals
+
+/-- **Single-occurrence count.**  For a window that fits, exactly `b ^ (L - k)`
+volumes have the pattern occurring at position `i`. -/
+theorem card_occursAt {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (i : ℕ)
+    (h : i + k ≤ L) :
+    (Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Volume L b => occursAt p i v)).card = b ^ (L - k) := by
+  have := card_agree L b (windowFin L k i) (patExtend i p)
+  rw [windowFin_card L k i h] at this
+  convert this using 2
+
+/-! ## Positions and the occurrence count `X` -/
+
+/-- The set of valid starting positions for a length-`k` pattern in a length-`L`
+volume: `{i : i + k ≤ L}`.  Has `L - k + 1` elements when `k ≤ L`, and is empty
+when `k > L`. -/
+def positions (L k : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := (Finset.range (L + 1)).filter (fun i => i + k ≤ L)
+
+theorem mem_positions {L k i : ℕ} : i ∈ positions L k ↔ i + k ≤ L := by
+  unfold positions
+  simp only [mem_filter, Finset.mem_range]
+  omega
+
+theorem positions_card_of_le {L k : ℕ} (h : k ≤ L) : (positions L k).card = L - k + 1 := by
+  have hrange : positions L k = Finset.range (L - k + 1) := by
+    ext i; simp only [mem_positions, Finset.mem_range]; omega
+  rw [hrange, Finset.card_range]
+
+theorem positions_eq_empty_of_gt {L k : ℕ} (h : L < k) : positions L k = ∅ := by
+  rw [Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
+  intro i hi; rw [mem_positions] at hi; omega
+
+/-- The **occurrence count** `X = occCount p v`: the number of positions at which
+the pattern `p` occurs in the volume `v`. -/
+def occCount {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (v : Volume L b) : ℕ :=
+  ((positions L k).filter (fun i => occursAt p i v)).card
+
+/-- **Edge case `k > L`.**  A pattern longer than the volume never occurs, so
+`X = 0` deterministically. -/
+theorem occCount_eq_zero_of_gt {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b)
+    (v : Volume L b) (h : L < k) : occCount p v = 0 := by
+  unfold occCount
+  rw [positions_eq_empty_of_gt h]
+  simp
+
+/-- `X ≥ 1` exactly when the pattern occurs at some valid position. -/
+theorem occCount_pos_iff {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (v : Volume L b) :
+    0 < occCount p v ↔ ∃ i ∈ positions L k, occursAt p i v := by
+  unfold occCount
+  rw [Finset.card_pos, Finset.filter_nonempty_iff]
+
+/-! ## Part 1: Expectation -/
+
+/--
+**Total occurrence count over the library.**
+`Σ_v X(v) = (L - k + 1) · b^(L-k)` — double counting `(volume, position)` pairs.
+-/
+theorem sum_occCount {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (h : k ≤ L) :
+    ∑ v : Volume L b, occCount p v = (L - k + 1) * b ^ (L - k) := by
+  -- Rewrite the left-hand side using the definition of `occCount`.
+  have h_lhs :
+    ∑ v : Volume L b, occCount p v =
+    ∑ i ∈ positions L k, (Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Volume L b => occursAt p i v)).card := by
+      simp +decide only [occCount, card_filter];
+      exact Finset.sum_comm;
+  convert h_lhs using 1;
+  rw [ Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => card_occursAt p i <| by linarith [ mem_positions.mp hi ] ] ; simp +decide [ positions_card_of_le h ]
+
+/-- **Expectation** of a `ℚ`-valued statistic of a uniformly random volume. -/
+noncomputable def expectation {L b : ℕ} [NeZero b] (f : Volume L b → ℚ) : ℚ :=
+  (∑ v : Volume L b, f v) / (b ^ L : ℚ)
+
+/--
+**Expected number of occurrences.**  `E[X] = (L - k + 1) · b^{-k}`.
+-/
+theorem expectation_occCount {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (h : k ≤ L) :
+    expectation (fun v : Volume L b => (occCount p v : ℚ)) = (L - k + 1 : ℕ) / (b ^ k : ℚ) := by
+  convert congr_arg ( fun x : ℚ => x / ( b ^ L : ℚ ) ) ( show ( ∑ v : Volume L b, ( occCount p v : ℚ ) ) = ( L - k + 1 ) * b ^ ( L - k ) by
+                                                          rw_mod_cast [ sum_occCount p h ] ) using 1 ; ring;
+  rw [ show ( L : ℕ ) = k + ( L - k ) by rw [ Nat.add_sub_cancel' h ] ] ; norm_num [ pow_add ] ; ring;
+  simp +decide [ mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, NeZero.ne ];
+  rw [ mul_left_comm, mul_inv_cancel₀ ( pow_ne_zero _ ( NeZero.ne _ ) ), mul_one ]
+
+/-- **Edge case `k > L` for the expectation.**  `E[X] = 0`. -/
+theorem expectation_occCount_eq_zero_of_gt {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b)
+    (h : L < k) : expectation (fun v : Volume L b => (occCount p v : ℚ)) = 0 := by
+  unfold expectation
+  have : ∀ v : Volume L b, (occCount p v : ℚ) = 0 := by
+    intro v; rw [occCount_eq_zero_of_gt p v h]; simp
+  simp [this]
+
+/-! ## Probability and Part 2: Bonferroni bounds on `P(X ≥ 1)` -/
+
+/-- The **probability** of an event `A` for a uniformly random volume. -/
+noncomputable def prob {L b : ℕ} [NeZero b] (A : Volume L b → Prop) [DecidablePred A] : ℚ :=
+  ((Finset.univ.filter A).card : ℚ) / (b ^ L : ℚ)
+
+/-- The occurrence events: `occEvent p i` is the set of volumes in which `p`
+occurs at position `i`. -/
+def occEvent {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (i : ℕ) : Finset (Volume L b) :=
+  Finset.univ.filter (fun v => occursAt p i v)
+
+/--
+`{v : X(v) ≥ 1}` is the union of the occurrence events over all positions.
+-/
+theorem filter_occCount_pos_eq_biUnion {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) :
+    Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Volume L b => 0 < occCount p v)
+      = (positions L k).biUnion (fun i => occEvent p i) := by
+  ext v; simp [occEvent, occCount_pos_iff]
+
+/--
+**Union bound (first Bonferroni inequality).**
+`P(X ≥ 1) ≤ E[X] = (L - k + 1)·b^{-k}`.
+-/
+theorem prob_pos_le_expectation {L b k : ℕ} [NeZero b] (p : Fin k → Fin b) (h : k ≤ L) :
+    prob (fun v : Volume L b => 0 < occCount p v) ≤ (L - k + 1 : ℕ) / (b ^ k : ℚ) := by
+  rw [ prob ];
+  rw [ div_le_div_iff₀ ] <;> norm_cast;
+  · rw [ show b ^ L = b ^ ( L - k ) * b ^ k by rw [ ← pow_add, Nat.sub_add_cancel h ] ];
+    convert Nat.mul_le_mul_right ( b ^ k ) ( Finset.card_biUnion_le.trans ?_ ) using 1;
+    rw [ filter_occCount_pos_eq_biUnion ];
+    rw [ ← mul_assoc ];
+    convert Finset.sum_le_card_nsmul _ _ _ _;
+    · rw [ positions_card_of_le h ];
+    · infer_instance;
+    · intro i hi; rw [ show occEvent p i = Finset.univ.filter ( fun v => occursAt p i v ) by rfl ] ; rw [ card_occursAt p i ( by linarith [ mem_positions.mp hi ] ) ] ;
+  · exact pow_pos ( NeZero.pos b ) _;
+  · exact pow_pos ( NeZero.pos b ) _
+
+/--
+**Second Bonferroni inequality, combinatorial core.**  For any finite family
+of finite sets,
+`2·Σ|Eᵢ| ≤ 2·|⋃ Eᵢ| + Σ_{(i,j), i≠j} |Eᵢ ∩ Eⱼ|`,
+equivalently `|⋃ Eᵢ| ≥ Σ|Eᵢ| - Σ_{i<j}|Eᵢ ∩ Eⱼ|`.
+-/
+theorem bonferroni_lower {ι α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (s : Finset ι) (E : ι → Finset α) :
+    2 * ∑ i ∈ s, (E i).card
+      ≤ 2 * (s.biUnion E).card + ∑ q ∈ s.offDiag, (E q.1 ∩ E q.2).card := by
+  -- Let `U := s.biUnion E` be the ambient finset; for `i ∈ s`, `E i ⊆ U`. For `a : α` define `d a := (s.filter (fun i => a ∈ E i)).card`.
+  set U := s.biUnion E
